title: Mutual Exclusion
body:
At most one process in a critical section at a time

The first of the three requirements for solving the [[Critical Section Problem]], alongside
[[Progress]] and [[Bounded Waiting]]. It is the one everybody remembers, and on its own it
is not enough: a solution that blocks *every* thread forever satisfies mutual exclusion
perfectly and is useless. That is what the other two requirements are for.

"At most one" is about the resource, not about the code. Two threads running two *different*
functions that both write the same global are in the same critical section as far as this
requirement is concerned. The section is defined by the shared data it touches.

Every mechanism in the course is a way of enforcing it:

| Mechanism | Enforces it by |
|---|---|
| [[Peterson's Solution]] | `flag[]` and `turn`, in software only |
| [[TAS]] | one atomic instruction that no other thread can interleave with |
| [[Mutex Lock]] | a binary [[Semaphores\|semaphore]]: 0 means taken, 1 means free |
| [[Semaphores]] | a counter; set it to 1 and you have mutual exclusion, set it to *n* and you have something else |

The `mutex` semaphore in the [[Bounded Buffer Problem]] is initialised to 1 for exactly this
reason.
